Two examined wallets: recorded Aave debt, collateral and
repayment rights
Research date: 29 September 2026. This is a getter-only public-state audit with retrospective
interpretation of an existing repayment-log census. It submits no transactions, constructs no repayment
or liquidation transaction, and performs no state-changing simulation.
Findings
The examined address 0xe6Df4Ca976F3feC8DA89EfEc332dC2245F0a86Ff does have very large recorded debt in the
sampled copied Aave V3 pool. Its variable-debt balances include approximately 136.369 million DAI,
260.160 million USDC, 186.361 million USDT and 43.154 million WBTC. The WBTC liability dominates its
aggregate oracle valuation. Its sole nonzero aT oken holding among the 17 reserves is approximately
105,219.941 aWETH, enabled as collateral.
The second address, 0x6e3BF3c7bD91144D694621298cB8dA370479A7bb, has recorded DAI, USDC and USDT debt and
holds aWETH/acbETH collateral. It also appears in the earlier public repayment census. Neither address
has a healthy borrow position under the pool's sampled oracle accounting: both health factors are far
below one. These are on-chain accounting facts, not market valuations or evidence identifying a human
owner.
Repaying another account's ordinary borrow reduces that account's debt. It does not by itself transfer its
collateral, ownership, borrowing rights or remaining aT okens to the payer. Portal backing and ordinary
borrower repayment remain separate accounting operations. A profit claim requires an independently
established right to receive assets and realizable proceeds exceeding every funding cost; the existence
of a large debt balance establishes neither.
pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 128

Scope, provenance and decoding
All new chain reads use PulseChain chain 369, block 27,659,393, hash 
0xc5e582cd902f4bff3b1aa325b9b564fcd5d6dc0ffa77a03fcd105b65c6390275, timestamp 28 September 2026
08:22:35 UTC. The header was rechecked after each batch. The V3 pool is 
0x87870bca3f3fd6335c3f4ce8392d69350b4fa4e2. The reserve list comes from the same-block recorded 
getReservesList census, and getReserveData identifies each reserve's aT oken, stable-debt token, variable-
debt token and reserve ID. Balances are actual balanceOf results on those contracts; they are not inferred
from explorer labels or transfers.
The 17 reserves examined are WETH, wstETH, WBTC, USDC, DAI, LINK, AAVE, cbETH, USDT, rETH, LUSD,
CRV, MKR, SNX, BAL, UNI and LDO. Their underlying decimals and symbols were read directly. MKR uses
a bytes32 symbol response, while the other sampled responses use the ABI dynamic-string
representation. WBTC has eight decimals, USDC/USDT six, and the remaining reserves eighteen. The
collateral flags are decoded from getUserConfiguration, using bit 2 × reserveId + 1; the borrowing flag uses
bit 2 × reserveId. Both wallets report eMode zero.
The provider's returned oracle is 0x54586be62e3c3580375ae3723c145253060ca0c2. Its BASE_CURRENCY is the zero
address and its BASE_CURRENCY_UNIT is 100,000,000. Account-data values below are divided by that unit;
health factors are divided by 10^18. A zero-address base convention does not provide external dollar
redemption or establish that copied token market prices agree with the oracle. Feed freshness and
external market depth were not audited in this bounded batch.
As a consistency check, both aggregate debt values match exactly the sum of floor(variableDebtRaw ×
oraclePriceRaw / 10^underlyingDecimals) across reserves. The enabled-collateral holdings similarly reconcile
exactly to reported total collateral. This independently ties the account totals to the individual receipt/
debt-token reads. All 34 stable-debt balance reads return zero.
Aggregate account data
Value e6Df…86Ff 6e3B…A7bb
Collateral, oracle base units 193,537,665.46258272 10,684,216.39305430
Debt, oracle base units 1,234,186,253,416.83358896 82,673,116.84503121

points
8,250 8,249
LTV, basis points 8,000 7,999
Health factor 0.000129371538181202 0.106605513847397546
These interest-bearing liabilities are not a measure of tokens currently held by the borrower, the amount
originally borrowed, or tokens newly minted in a single transaction. An origination chronology and
interest-index decomposition would be needed to establish how each balance developed. This audit does
not infer that the 43.154-million-WBTC debt corresponds to that many WBTC transferred at origination.
Reserve-specific positions
Only nonzero positions are printed below; each omitted asset had zero aT oken, stable-debt and variable-
debt balances for that wallet in the complete census. The aT oken values are underlying-denominated
Aave claims, not static wa-wrapper share quantities. Every stable-debt balance is zero. Receipt/debt
contract addresses and raw integer amounts remain in the retained batch.

Collateral availability and repayment meaning
Actual WETH cash in its aT oken contract is 1,649,712.575569873755878469 WETH; actual cbETH
cash is 42,200.252108978475003934 cbETH. Both exceed the respective combined aT oken holdings
of these two wallets at this snapshot. Thus a blanket claim that all collateral reserves have no cash
would be incorrect. Conversely, DAI, USDC and USDT cash is zero. Reserve cash and a wallet's right to
withdraw it are separate conditions.
The verified V3 SupplyLogic.executeWithdraw burns the caller's aT okens, transfers underlying to the selected
recipient and applies the collateral health-factor/LTV validation when borrowing remains. The burn and
transfer are within the same transaction: a later validation failure reverts the transaction. 
SupplyLogic.executeFinalizeTransfer also subjects a collateral aT oken transfer to health validation when the
sender has borrowing. Calling a generic token withdrawal function on a separate contract does not
remove these Aave checks. Verified V3 source and dependencies.
Repayment can improve health and, if sufficiently large under the applicable prices and parameters,
make some collateral withdrawable by its rightful holder. The exact amount depends on the entire
remaining debt/collateral position, the asset being withdrawn and current validation rules. Reducing debt
by a small amount does not automatically free the same amount of collateral, especially for these
severely undercollateralized oracle-accounting positions.
In the verified BorrowLogic.executeRepay, underlying repayment transfers the payer's actual underlying to
the reserve aT oken contract and burns the beneficiary's selected debt. It does not transfer the
beneficiary's collateral to the payer. A distinct liquidation operation has distinct rules and effects; it must
not be described as ordinary repay(onBehalfOf) ownership acquisition. Credit delegation likewise authorizes
borrowing subject to its own rules; it is not an ordinary ERC-20 transfer of an existing debt balance. 
Verified BorrowLogic and SupplyLogic.
The representative DAI variable-debt token is 0xcf8d0c70c850859266f5c338b38f9d663181c314. Its implementation
slot at the pinned block identifies 0xac725cb59d16c81061bdea61041a8a5e73da9ec6. The verified VariableDebtToken
implementation explicitly reverts with OPERATION_NOT_SUPPORTED in transfer, transferFrom, approve, allowance and
allowance adjustment methods. Its balance records debt attributed to an account; it is not a freely
transferable asset that a caller can take from a contract and thereby acquire collateral ownership. 
Verified variable-debt implementation.
The DAI stable-debt token's sampled implementation is 0x15c5620dffac7c7366eed66c20ad222ddbb1ed57; the
explorer returned an address-only record without verified source. This study therefore does not claim an
equally verified current implementation-level transfer proof for that contract. Both wallets' stable-debt
holdings are zero. Nor does the representative DAI source check constitute a full implementation census
of all 34 debt-token contracts; the complete balance census and the source-check scope are distinct.
The further claim that e6Df…86Ff is a contract with a publicly callable token-withdrawal facility requires
separate bytecode/source and access-control evidence. These balance getters neither establish nor
refute that behavior. Even if such a facility exists, it does not by itself override transfer restrictions of the
requested token or collateral validation in Aave. Any claim that a caller receives valuable assets after
paying the contract's debt must establish that entitlement separately.
Existing post-fork repayment evidence
The existing V3 census covers blocks 17,233,000–27,659,393, using the standard 
Repay(address,address,address,uint256,bool) signature. Its indexed addresses distinguish reserve, beneficiary
and repayer. No new broad log query was needed for this wallet audit.
pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 131

No returned standard Repay event names e6Df…86Ff as either beneficiary or repayer. This is compatible
with its present debt and does not imply zero debt, no original borrowing, or no other debt-changing
operation. For 6e3B…A7bb, 29 returned logs match at least one of those roles:
Role of 6e3B…A7bb Asset Events Gross recorded amount
Repayer USDT 9 2,161,000
Repayer USDC 16 380,000
Debt beneficiary USDT 8 2,160,000
Debt beneficiary USDC 16 380,000
Debt beneficiary DAI 4 0.000000000000000444
The role totals overlap and must not be added as independent payments. The USDT difference includes
a 1,000-USDT payment by 6e3B…A7bb for another account, c000…fd34. It demonstrates third-party
repayment, not an associated collateral-ownership transfer. Verified example receipt.
The DAI total is 444 raw wei. One 111-wei payment on behalf of 6e3B…A7bb generated a debt-token
Mint event of approximately 4.805 million DAI because previously accrued interest exceeded the tiny
repayment. The mint-event magnitude is not the amount paid. The earlier study reconciles interest,
transfer and debt events in the receipt. Example DAI receipt, repayment-history study (Appendix 9).
Both bounded V2 getUserAccountData calls at 0x7d2768de32b0b80b7a3454c06bdac94a69ddc7a9 revert. The prior study
records post-fork implementation changes at that pool. These failed getters establish unavailable
standard-interface results, not zero V2 positions. This study makes no V2 position valuation.
Implication for the proposed Portal and arbitrage interpretation
These results strengthen the factual premise that some examined addresses have large outstanding
borrow liabilities and collateral claims. They do not prove that those liabilities were acquired by
transferring debt tokens, that a payer can obtain the collateral, or that the claims have realizable
external-dollar value.
Ordinary repayment replaces a reserve loan claim with actual reserve cash; Portal backing reduces
reserve-level unbacked issuance. Paying one balance does not automatically settle the other. A newly
issued aT oken sold to a pool leaves that pool holding an Aave claim. A subsequent repayment of a third
party's borrow may add reserve cash, but its economic cost and the separately outstanding Portal
balance remain in the accounting. The same token proceeds cannot fund both commitments twice.
A profitable arbitrage is therefore conditional on realizable relative prices, full settlement costs, fees,
inventory, and an enforceable entitlement to the assets eventually received. Neither a large debt getter
nor a public repayment function proves those conditions. The read-only findings support precise
accounting analysis; they do not establish a completed self-funding cycle. Portal accounting study
(Appendix 17).
Reproduction references
The maintained explicit getter manifests are Research/experiments/parb_wallet_debt_metadata_20260929.json and
Research/experiments/parb_wallet_debt_balances_20260929.json, with the bounded source-provenance lookup in 
Research/experiments/parb_wallet_debt_implementations_20260929.json. Run each with Research/scripts/
probe_pulsechain_routes.py, explicit --block 0x1a60c81, --calls pointing to that manifest and a fresh --output
path. The explicit manifests contain getters only; this study does not use the runner's default experiment
mode. Existing result paths are preserved.
pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 132

Ignored raw evidence is under artifacts/parb-wallet-debt-positions-20260929/: metadata.json, balances.json,
decoded summary.json and repayment_matches.json. The latter derives only from the already recorded 
artifacts/parb-debt-history-20260929/V3_repay_logs.json. The implementation/source records supporting
token-transfer semantics, where available, are retained in the same batch. Exact raw results, addresses,
header hashes and errors remain available there; this study prints the decision-relevant positions rather
than embedding source or the entire response catalogue.
pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 133
